articles.title: Farewell, Cybertruck: why the winding down of the ‘Maga hat on wheels’ is a sign of the times
articles.summary: Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party. It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse.
body: Three days after a historic blue tsunami changed America’s political landscape, Elon Musk announced Tesla would end production of its hulking Cybertruck next year.

Was it a coincidence? Maybe. Musk said the move was “to make room for increased Cybercab production”, referring to Tesla’s Robotaxi. But the combined circumstances felt highly appropriate: it was the end of an era.

Eccentric and overhyped, the Cybertruck became a kind of automotive stand-in for Musk himself amid his political ascent. Like so many of his projects, it was massively promoted, heavily delayed, and ultimately fell short: Musk once predicted he could sell 250,000 a year but ultimately sold 70,000 in three years, losing $1.9bn in the process, according to Quartz.
points: Eccentric and overhyped, Tesla’s Cybertruck became a stand-in for Elon Musk during his ascent in the Republican party.
It will join the ranks of other vehicles symbolic of their eras – for better or for worse.

articles.title: ‘Pretty weird’: How a viral video shows a striking discrepancy in men and women’s knitwear
articles.summary: Men are routinely getting more wool for their money – are women really paying a pink tax when they buy a jumper? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here. It’s officially cosy season.
body: It’s officially cosy season. But before you treat yourself to a new wooly jumper, you may want to take a closer look at the care label.
Abercrombie & Fitch is facing a pink tax backlash, sparked by a video on TikTok that highlights the difference between the materials used in menswear and womenswear jumpers that cost the same.

Last month, while browsing the American brand’s site, Rachael Brownfield, a fashion content creator, noticed that it was selling a 100% merino wool jumper in its menswear section for $95 (£71), while a jumper for the same price in the womenswear section consisted of only 30% wool. While the styles of jumpers are different, they were marketed alongside each other in a social media post.

“Pretty weird,” she wrote below a video in which she questioned why a synthetic women’s jumper should cost the same as a men’s jumper made of pure wool. The Guardian has approached Abercrombie & Fitch for comment.

articles.title: Before Anything Else, Geoffrey Holder Was a Painter. A New Show Spotlights His Tremendous Body of Work
articles.summary: Guest curated by Dr. Erica Moiah James, the Museum of Contemporary Art North Miami’s “Geoffrey Holder: Black Magic” is the first museum survey to center the Tony-winning multihyphenate’s work as a visual artist.
body: Geoffrey Holder refused to choose a lane. Born in Trinidad and Tobago in 1930, he was a principal dancer with the Metropolitan Opera Ballet, the first Black man to win Tony Awards for both directing and costume design (for the Broadway hit The Wiz ), and the voice and face of 7Up throughout the 1970s and ’80s, all while building a celebrated film career with roles in Doctor Dolittle, Annie, and the Bond film Live and Let Die.

And yet, before everything else, Holder was a painter. “Painting always came first,” says his son, Leo Holder, who oversees the artist’s estate. “Practically everything else he did has always been an extension of this. He was always working on something. At any given time, wherever he was living, there were several canvases in progress.” Still, across his decades-long career, it was the facet of his work that received the least attention.

articles.title: Experience: I was disembowelled by a hippo on my honeymoon
articles.summary: A mother hippopotamus protecting her young is one of the most fearsome forces of nature. Luckily, I’d just married someone ready to meet it head-on. Anna and I got married in Portugal in September last year. We had been together for 13 years.
body: Ten days later, I found myself in a swamp in Botswana with my intestines hanging out of my back.
We were on our honeymoon in the Okavango Delta. That evening, we had set off with a group in traditional canoes. We weren’t looking for hippos; the excursion was supposed to be about plants.

Before we left, we were warned that a mother hippo with two babies was nearby, so we would stay away from her. I spotted the hippo in the distance and zoomed in to take a photo – she was huge, her open mouth showing big teeth; the calves were behind her.

Our canoe had drifted away from the others. Suddenly, I heard a noise behind us – splashing, grunting, growling. The boat started rocking. I turned to my left and saw the same hippo, mouth still open, charging. The look on the guide’s face was one I will never forget: sheer terror.
points: A mother hippopotamus protecting her young is one of the most fearsome forces of nature.
Luckily, I’d just married someone ready to meet it head-on.
Anna and I got married in Portugal in September last year.
We were on our honeymoon in the Okavango Delta.

articles.title: Rosalía Co-Signs One of This Year’s Most Viral Looks at the Latin Grammys
articles.summary: From a sculptural Matières Fécales confection to custom Erdem and Vivienne Westwood, Rosalía’s Latin Grammys wardrobe was a masterclass in high-fashion fantasy.
body: Rosalía is having a heavenly year, and she has the wardrobe to match. At last night’s Latin Grammy Awards in Las Vegas, the Spanish superstar, who took home a suite of awards including Album of the Year for Lux and Song of the Year for “La Perla,” delivered a series of fantastical, sent-from-above fashion moments.

First up? A gloriously frothy white creation from Matières Fécales, one of the year’s most talked-about—and increasingly celebrity-beloved—fashion labels. Styled by Chloe and Chenelle, Rosalía arrived in a custom gown inspired by the Paris-based label’s spring 2027 collection. The look featured a sheer, tightly ruched corset bodice, clouds of tulle billowing around the shoulders, and an enormous, floor-sweeping skirt. It compounded much of the star’s ongoing aesthetic, which oscillates between bridal confection, prima ballerina, and celestial apparition. Right at home in the spiritually charged universe of Lux.
points: From a sculptural Matières Fécales confection to custom Erdem and Vivienne Westwood, Rosalía’s Latin Grammys wardrobe was a masterclass in high-fashion fantasy.

articles.title: The 5 Wellness Trends That Will Define 2027
articles.summary: Personalization, light as a supplement, and a “less is more” approach; industry leaders and analysts unpack the trends set to define wellness in 2027.
body: In 2026, wellness hit new heights. We maxxed protein and creatine and leveled up our supplement stacks. GLP-1s were seemingly everywhere, so was the topic of peptides. As optimization dominated the conversation, a backlash simultaneously grew. Longevity remained a core pursuit, on land and at sea, aided by innovations in tech.

“The tectonic plates in culture are shifting under our feet,” says Lestat McCree, co-founder and CEO of UK-based wellness retailer Healf. “We say that the run club is now becoming the new nightclub, and weekends are full of saunas and ice baths. [Wellness is] the cultural mainstream, and people are really seeing this as the new way to live.”
Young consumers are gravitating towards in-person micro-communities. It’s an opportunity for agencies and brands that get it right.
points: Personalization, light as a supplement, and a “less is more” approach; industry leaders and analysts unpack the trends set to define wellness in 2027.
